## Why

Adeo Nota addresses a rebellion where both spiritual and temporal authorities were violently overthrown by the very subjects who should have obeyed them. I chose the Broken Scepter because it perfectly captures the fractured nature of both the papal spiritual authority over the clergy and the princely temporal authority over the territory of Avignon. The splintered wood and damaged metal clearly show the active rejection and violence against the established order that Pius VI condemns, while the remaining form asserts the inherent legitimacy and memory of that broken authority. This single, recognizable object embodies the central conflict far more clearly than any abstract representation of power or illegality could.

## Text-to-image prompt

A single, fractured sculptural depiction of a medieval European scepter, rendered as a fractured, broken artifact, is presented dead-center against a transparent background. The sculpture, crafted from aged, dark hardwood and tarnished gold, is split violently down its shaft into two jagged, uneven pieces. The upper third, holding the intricate finial shaped as a stylized fleur-de-lis, is completely severed from the lower two-thirds of the grip, showing the raw, splintered grain of the interior wood. The gold plating is scuffed, dented, and peeling away from the metal substrate, emphasizing age, neglect, and conflict. Procedural surface imperfections, including scratches and corrosion on the metal and deep fractures in the wood, provide rich micro-texture. This broken scepter rests on a simple, dark circular plinth of unpolished basalt stone. The camera is locked at 85mm, dead-center, frontal view, with a narrow f/11 aperture. Lighting is high-contrast and dramatic, with a strong key light from above-front-left and a rim light from rear-right, casting deep shadows within the fractures and crevices, while catching specular highlights on the tarnished gold surfaces and splintered wood. Pronounced ambient occlusion defines the complex broken geometry. The image is a premium Houdini/Octane render, emphasizing physically based materials and refined geometry. There is no text, environment, or background scene.
